_about: 747-400F, from Boeing D6-58326-1 Rev F (December 2024) 2.2.2 General Dimensions: Model 747-400 Freighter, -400ER Freighter (page index 31), drawn 8.4% larger than 2.2.1's 747-400: rasterized at scale 19.372 and clipped so its raster lies on the 747-400's (b744-passenger/) pixel for pixel, the same references serve. Its outlines are the 747-400's but for the shorter upper deck (placed here); the plan and front are the 747-400's sheet's (the same wing, tail and nacelles). The sheet draws the nose cargo door raised: the closed nose's outline under it is followed, and the door isn't a box the format holds (left out). No cabin windows drawn; doors from this drawing's outlines: the forward crew door, the aft door, the main-deck side cargo door (left), lower cargo doors and the bulk door (right: D6-58326-1 2.7.6-2.7.8 draw them in right side views). The windshield's forward edge, drawn up to 18 cm under the outline, is put on it (windshieldTolerance 0.2: Boeing draws its panes low).

windows.note: The 747-400F has no main-deck cabin windows, and its sheet draws none on the upper deck. A passenger 747-400 (also B744) is shapes/B744-passenger.json.

sources.title: Boeing, 747-400 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58326-1 Rev F, December 2024), 2.2.2 General Dimensions: Model 747-400 Freighter, -400ER Freighter, and 2.2.1 (plan and front views)
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side view of 2.2.2 and the plan and front views of 2.2.1 (tools/trace/b744/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. 2.2.2 draws the 747-400F 8.4% larger than 2.2.1 draws the 747-400; at their own scales the two side views lie on each other but for the upper deck, so the shape is the 747-400's (shapes/B744-passenger.json) with the freighter's shorter upper deck (fuselage.hump, from 5.5 m to 22.6 m) and its doors. No cabin windows are drawn. The nose cargo door is drawn raised and is left out (the format's doors are boxes); the main-deck side cargo door is on the left. This sheet prints the outboard engines 20.83 m out (2.2.1: 21 m, the same wing); the drawing's 21.18 m is +1.7% on it. The other checks and notes are the 747-400's.
